rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **principle of superposition** extends Coulomb's law to many charges: the force on any one charge is the **vector sum** of the independent pairwise forces $\frac{kq_iq_j}{r_{ij}^2}$ exerted by all the others — no pair is affected by a third charge's presence.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - F₁ = Σ F₁ᵢ (vector sum) - F = kq₁q₂/r² per pair - Equilateral triangle (like q): F_each = √3 kq²/a²

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Forces are vectors:** equal and opposite pairwise forces cancel even though each is large.  ·  **Independence of pairs:** other charges never "screen" a pairwise Coulomb force.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A sketched sign convention is part of the data.  ·  A dimensionless ratio still needs the two quantities named.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Midpoint of a like pair*** — net force zero by symmetry.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Charges +9 μC and +4 μC are 0.5 m apart. Where on the line between them is the net force on a third charge zero?** — 9/x² = 4/(0.5−x)² → 3/x = 2/(0.5−x) → x = 0.3 m from the 9 μC charge.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Superposition is electrostatics' algebra** — every multi-charge problem reduces to two-charge laws plus vector addition.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: F_net = vector sum of pairwise Coulomb forces.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The same superposition principle later builds electric fields, potentials and even quantum amplitudes.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Superposition: Adding Forces Vectorially With three or more charges, every pair interacts independently. Coulomb's law plus the **principle of superposition** — add all pairwise forces as vectors — handles any configuration, from electron clouds to charged spheres.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Principle of superposition The force on any charge in a system equals the **vector sum** of the forces each other charge would exert alone: $$\vec{F}_1 = \vec{F}_{12} + \vec{F}_{13} + \vec{F}_{14} + \cdots$$ - Each pairwise force obeys Coulomb's law independently — the presence of other charges does not modify any single pair's force.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 85:** superposition takes Coulomb's two-charge law as its building block. - **To electric field (Unit 20):** the same superposition principle applies to field vectors. - **To vectors (Unit 2):** component resolution is the practical tool.
